newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian 3rd GSM licence to cost abt nine bln bfr.
newsitem.headline: Belgian 3rd GSM licence to cost abt nine bln bfr.

text.p: The future operator of a third GSM mobile phone network in Belgium will have to pay about nine billion francs for the licence to the Belgian state, Deputy Prime Minister Elio di Rupo said on Friday.
"The price of the third licence will be comparable to the one paid by the two existing operators," Di Rupo said after the weekly cabinet meeting.

Since the third network would use the DCS 1800 technology, which requires more investment in the antenna network than is the case for other, existing technology, the amount might be revised down, he added.
The government said earlier on Friday it was inviting operators to enter bids for a third GSM mobile telephone network in Belgium.
The winner is to be selected within a year and the network is to be operational within two years.

Mobistar NV launched Belgium's second GSM network last August. Mobistar is 57 percent owned by France Telecom. Belgian data communications company Telinfo holds 10 percent and nine other Belgian companies the balance.
Belgium's first mobile service Proximus is run by Belgacom Mobile, 75-percent owned by Belgian state telephone operator Belgacom and 25-percent by AirTouch Communications Inc.
Belgium has more than half a million GSM users, with Mobistar accounting for about a fifth.
